text:
sre-bot: INCIDENT created — tokenizer preproc CPU spike causing pod OOMs in us-west-2. Potential customer impact: request 5xx for /v1/chat and tokenization timeouts. Auto-escalated to oncall. Severity: SEV2. pagerduty: https://pd.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

maya: saw repeated OOM kills on tokenizer pods, nodes flapping. Noticed spikes around 10:08 UTC where cpu usage jumped to 95% and kernel OOM killed processes.

maya: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=tokenizer -o wide` shows many restarts (RESTARTS > 20).

jon: looking. can you paste a pod log?

maya: pasted snippet from pod tokenizer-7889c:```
2026-02-18T10:08:12Z ERROR tokenizer: tokenization loop exceeded budget, input_len=240000, token_buffer_alloc failed: unable to allocate 52428800 bytes
2026-02-18T10:08:13Z INFO kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (tokenizer) total-vm:505000kB, anon-rss:490000kB
2026-02-18T10:08:13Z CRIT systemd: container exited with code 137
```

priya: this looks like pathological prompts — a customer test harness sent huge multi-MB prompts that trigger the C tokenizer to allocate large temporary buffers. We saw similar but not as severe in staging a month ago.

lee: support reports ~7 customers saw spike of 5xx between 10:07–10:12 UTC, no PII exposed. Customer A experienced ~30 requests fail, Customer B ~12.

maya: mitigation plan I'm trying now: 1) add temporary rate-limit on tokenization endpoint (drop/429 for >5 rps per IP) 2) scale tokenizer deployment to 0/rollout to a throttled image variant 3) apply pod memory limit bump 4) route traffic to fallback tokenizer model in us-east for critical customers.

jon: +1 for rate-limit. Also can we enable prefix-drop for oversized inputs as emergency: `max_input_bytes=200000` with `truncate_mode=prefix`?

priya: I can patch runtime to short-circuit very long inputs before calling into the C tokenizer. Push a hotfix to image `tokenizer:hotfix-1778` that checks input length and returns 413 / suggest chunking.

deploy-bot: Starting rollout: Deployment/tokenizer -> image=tokenizer:hotfix-1778, strategy=rolling (maxUnavailable=1)

maya: executing helm patch to inject rate-limit config on gateway: `helm upgrade gateway --set rateLimit.tokenize=5`

(5 minutes pass)

james? (note: noise)

jon: after initial rate-limit and deploy, observed reduction in CPU pressure. Still seeing a few pods crash during initial rollout. Applying memory bump to resource limits on the hottest node pools.

maya: cordoning node ip-10-2-44-12 that showed repeated oom_kill: `kubectl cordon ip-10-2-44-12` and draining tokenizers off it.

priya: hotfix image includes an early return and logs `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` for oversized requests. Pushed and rollout at 10:23 UTC.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete — tokenizer:hotfix-1778 -> 5/5 ready

maya: verifying metrics — tokenization latency P50 down from 2.3s to 0.45s, CPU usage on tokenizer pool back to 30-40%.

lee: support notif draft to customers: "We observed a short-lived incident affecting tokenization that caused request errors between 10:07–10:18 UTC. We mitigated by rolling a hotfix and applying rate limits. If you saw failed requests, please retry; no data loss. Apologies for the disruption." Approving?

jon: approve, add note about suggested mitigation for customers sending large synthetic prompts: chunking, smaller batch sizes.

maya: oncall handoff: @jon you're primary now. I'll head out to standup in 10.

jon: taking oncall — will monitor for 2 hours, then will hand back to maya if stable.

sre-bot: Reminder: create incident/SEV2 ticket and attach logs, timeline, customer impact.

maya: timeline quick draft: 10:07 UTC — spike begins; 10:08 UTC — first pod OOMs; 10:12 UTC — PD alert; 10:15 UTC — rate limit applied; 10:23 UTC — hotfix rollout complete; 10:35 UTC — metrics stable.

priya: root cause hypothesis: unbounded prompt payloads leading to pathologic behavior in tokenizer C implementation (buffer allocation + regex backtracking). Fix: defensive input validation in runtime + tokenizer library patch to pre-validate lengths and use streaming tokenizer for extremely long sequences.

jon: immediate action items: 1) postmortem (owner: maya) 2) library patch PR (owner: priya) 3) automated test with fuzzed long inputs (owner: eng-ml) 4) add a hard-enforced gateway input size limit (owner: eng-platform)

lee: support: will notify affected customers with the approved message and offer help re: retries.

maya: adding tags: `incident:tokenizer`, `region:us-west-2`, `cause:input-size`, `sev:2`.

jon: monitoring — if we see another spike, fallback to model-compact tokenizer variant and escalate to SEV1.

sre-bot: oncall handoff recorded: from maya -> jon at 10:40 UTC.

maya: thanks team — leaving notes in ops-runbook. I'll own the postmortem write-up and link to PRs.

lee: closing notes: total customer impact small but visible; recommend follow-up discussion in next reliability sync. :thumbsup:
